item.title: Plans for national nickel hub revealed by Kumul Minerals
item.description: Kumul Minerals Holdings Limited is planning a national nickel hub in Madang province as part of a wider strategy to process more of Papua New Guinea’s minerals domestically, instead of exporting partially processed products. Kumul Mineral Holdings Managing Director, Sarimu Kanu outlined the proposal during a question-and-answer session with Business Advantage International Publishing Director Andr
item.content:encoded:
Kumul Minerals Holdings Limited is planning a national nickel hub in Madang province as part of a wider strategy to process more of Papua New Guinea’s minerals domestically, instead of exporting partially processed products.

Kumul Mineral Holdings Managing Director, Sarimu Kanu outlined the proposal during a question-and-answer session with Business Advantage International Publishing Director Andrew Wilkins at the Business Advantage PNG Investment Conference in Brisbane on Tuesday.

Kanu said the proposed hub would be centred on the expansion of the Ramu nickel-cobalt operation and the construction of a refinery capable of producing nickel cathode and nickel sulphate.

“What is unique about that particular strategy in Ramu is that we are driving the expansion of Ramu from about 32,000 tonnes a year to about 74,000 tonnes of nickel produced a year,” Kanu said.

The proposed expansion, however, remains subject to regulatory approvals, agreements, financing and detailed development work.

Kanu said KMHL had acquired an interest in Ramu NiCo and was looking at acquiring a further interest in the project.

The Independent Consumer and Competition Commission announced earlier this year that it had cleared KMHL’s proposed acquisition of a 1.97 per cent participating interest in the Ramu Nickel Cobalt Joint Venture from Mineral Resources Ramu Limited.

Kanu told the conference that KMHL expected to acquire a further 20 per cent interest within the next few months, although he did not provide further details about the proposed transaction.

Ramu NiCo currently produces mixed hydroxide precipitate, or MHP, at its Basamuk processing plant.

Nickel cathode is used in manufacturing stainless steel, while nickel sulphate is an important material in battery production.

Kanu said the ultimate aim was to make nickel the first PNG base metal exported as a refined metal product.

“We want to aggregate all the nickel prospects in the country to feed into the refinery.

“We want to drive the strategy that nickel will be the first base metal that will be exported in metal cathode form. All the processing will be done in PNG.” He said.

The existing Basamuk processing plant and Kurumbukari mine could serve as foundation customers for new power developments.

Kanu said cheaper power could also help unlock the long-planned Madang Pacific Marine Industrial Zone, which would be difficult to operate competitively using diesel-generated electricity.

item.title: Hela expands water fleet to counter dry spell
item.description: The Hela provincial government has expanded its emergency drought response by purchasing four additional 10,000-liter water trucks, scheduled for delivery next month. This addition doubles the province's fleet to eight water tankers as the province copes with the intensifying El Niño drought.
item.content:encoded:
The Hela provincial government has expanded its emergency drought response by purchasing four additional 10,000-liter water trucks, scheduled for delivery next month.

This addition doubles the province's fleet to eight water tankers as the province copes with the intensifying El Niño drought.

​Hela governor Philip Undialu said the initial four trucks purchased have been operating around Tari Town, supplying water to government institutions, public servants, local churches, and nearby communities.

"With four more trucks arriving, the distribution strategy will expand across the province, allocating one water truck directly to each of the four districts to extend relief beyond the capital," he said.

​Undialu also warned customary landowners and local guardians of natural water sources to stop imposing fees or restricting public access during the severe dry spell.

​"Water is a universal human right," he said.

Undialu said anyone charging fees or blocking access during a drought could face legal consequences.

​He said natural water supplies located on private land must remain accessible to everyone in the community during this dry season.

​Governor Undialu confirmed that the Hela provincial disaster management committee has been established under National Disaster Centre’s directive.

He assured the public that the committee is working around the clock to coordinate relief efforts and safeguard communities throughout the ongoing disaster.

item.title: Starlink to boost emergency aid delivery in Milne Bay
item.description: Remote island communities and disaster officers in Milne Bay are set for faster emergency relief and real-time reporting following the delivery of new Starlink satellite communication equipment. The National Disaster Centre [NDC] provided a standard unit and a portable unit to the province on Wednesday to ensure critical communications remain online during the ongoing El Niño dry spell.
item.content:encoded:
Remote island communities and disaster officers in Milne Bay are set for faster emergency relief and real-time reporting following the delivery of new Starlink satellite communication equipment.

The National Disaster Centre [NDC] provided a standard unit and a portable unit to the province on Wednesday to ensure critical communications remain online during the ongoing El Niño dry spell.

The high-speed internet units will eliminate communication blackouts that have long delayed emergency assessments, relief supplies, and casualty updates from isolated outer islands during natural disasters.

NDC acting Director-General Lusete Laso Mana said fast, reliable communication directly impacts how quickly life-saving assistance reaches affected communities.

"El Niño is affecting many parts of the country and communication is becoming a challenge for us," Mana said.

"Some of the provinces, when contacted for reports or situational updates, do not respond promptly or do not respond at all."

He said the new satellite connection will ensure Milne Bay can transmit immediate situational reports to headquarters, allowing relief teams to deploy assistance without delay.

Milne Bay acting provincial administrator Sharon Mua said the technology brings immediate relief to provincial disaster teams who previously relied on aging VHF radio networks.

"On behalf of the provincial disaster committee and provincial government, we thank NDC for meeting our need," Mua said.

"We have been thinking of installing VHF radios because that has been working for us in the past. NDC seeing the need and bringing Starlink to our aid, we are grateful for the foresight."

The standard unit will serve as a permanent communications hub at the provincial administration office in Alotau, while the portable set will travel with emergency teams directly into disaster zones.

Milne Bay is among the first model provinces to receive the technology under an NDC initiative that will distribute 36 Starlink sets to emergency centers across the nation.

item.title: Road link to end Nomad isolation
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has opened one of Western’s most isolated outposts, launching major infrastructure developments in Nomad, Middle Fly. Nomad Station came alive yesterday with traditional dancing and live entertainment as Marape launched the Kiunga-Nomad Road construction, breaking decades of geographical isolation by connecting the remote district directly to Kiunga’s commercial hub.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has opened one of Western’s most isolated outposts, launching major infrastructure developments in Nomad, Middle Fly.

Nomad Station came alive yesterday with traditional dancing and live entertainment as Marape launched the Kiunga-Nomad Road construction, breaking decades of geographical isolation by connecting the remote district directly to Kiunga’s commercial hub.

PM Marape also launched the construction of the new Middle Fly District Administration Building and witnessed the maiden financial transaction at the newly established Nomad District Treasury Office.

The local treasury ends years of administrative delay, allowing district funds to be processed directly on site rather than through distant provincial centers.

Speaking during the historic first cheque printing, Marape urged finance officials to push towards digital operations.

"Well done. This is the first cheque to come out here, and I look forward to many more," PM said.

"More importantly, finance officials will work with the Department of Finance to migrate beyond cheques to direct electronic transactions from this station."

District leaders hailed the combined road link, administration hub, and local treasury as a major breakthrough in decentralizing government authority and bringing basic services to rural Middle Fly.

Marape was accompanied by provincial leaders and government delegates during the official launch.

item.title: Madang provincial hospital scales down services
item.description: The Madang provincial hospital will begin an indefinite scaling down of its services today due to a critical shortage of essential medical drugs and other consumables. Chief executive officer of the Madang Provincial Health Authority, Dr Martin Daimen, announced through a circular yesterday that the management has taken this drastic measure due to the ongoing shortage of essential drugs at the pro
item.content:encoded:
The Madang provincial hospital will begin an indefinite scaling down of its services today due to a critical shortage of essential medical drugs and other consumables.

Chief executive officer of the Madang Provincial Health Authority, Dr Martin Daimen, announced through a circular yesterday that the management has taken this drastic measure due to the ongoing shortage of essential drugs at the provincial hospital.

The decision to scale down services was reached on Tuesday during a meeting of the hospital's senior executive management team.

Dr. Daimen explained that these measures will remain effective until such time there are adequate medical supplies in stock.

"The management decided to scale down some services and operations in certain areas of the hospital due to the constant shortages of vital and essential medical drugs, plus other items at the Area Medical Store in Lae," he said.

"The decision was made in order to reserve the limited medical drugs and consumables for very critically ill patients until normal supplies are received from the AMS in Lae."

In the meantime, Dr. Daimen added that the management is working on acquiring some medical items to supplement the supplies and is also seeking assistance from partners and stakeholders to assist where possible.

During this period, Dr. Daimen outlined the following measures would be taken at the respective sections of the hospital.

For the Public Outpatient and Dental Clinic, Dr Daimen said services should focus on emergency cases only but should assist the public with prescriptions to buy medicines at private pharmacies in town.

However, he stated that all emergency referrals must be first communicated to the emergency physician and his delegate for further action to be taken. He added that ambulatory service is also suspended and will attend to emergencies only to be attended to by the respective specialist team.

Day clinics, including TB, HIV and dental, will remain open to the public requiring prescriptions for medication. TB and HIV clinics should be opened to serve medicines to continuing patients only.

For the Labour ward, the CEO said it is unable to operate without specialist medical supplies, hence is unable to cater for all patients currently, and therefore; we appeal to all normal cases to seek services at the Yagaum Lutheran Health Centre or the Catholic- run Alexishafen Health Centre, or any nearest clinics convenient to them.

The Emergencies and Operating Theatre will suspend all elective surgeries, and focus will be given to emergencies only. Patients are encouraged to purchase critical items from retail pharmacies during this time.

Meanwhile, all hospital wards are being directed to discharge all stable patients immediately and attention given to critically ill patients only. Hospital ambulances can assist repatriate patients along the highways only or within an hour of driving.

The radiology and pathology units should be opened to inpatients and emergencies only during this time, whilst the hospital pharmacy will be opened as usual but may reserve medicines for inpatients and discharged patients only. Most patients will be required to purchase medicines from retail pharmacies in town.

For the physiotherapy, Dr Daimen said it will be opened to the general public, but staff will attend to hospitalised patients only.

The CEO also emphasised that all staff are required to be at their respective work stations on official hours of duty or as per shift rosters to assist the general public where possible.

Dr Daimen urged the Hospital Executive Management and responsible managers to ensure the above measures are implemented accordingly and that they must provide feedback in a timely manner until such time the situation at the hospital improves.

The Madang Provincial Referral Hospital is a level facility that takes in referrals from neighbouring provinces of East Sepik, Manus, and Morobe.

It is also used as a teaching and learning hospital by students from the Medical Faculty of Divine Word University, nursing students from the Lutheran School of Nursing, which is now a campus of the Lutheran University, as well as students from the PNG Maritime College.

item.title: Goroka contractor rebrands PNG DataCo facilities
item.description: Goroka-based contractor Mebiluba Service and Maintenance has commenced refurbishment and rebranding work on PNG DataCo's Kumul Submarine Cable Network landing facility in Alotau, Milne Bay. The six-man team from Eastern Highlands has been engaged to rebrand DataCo facilities across Papua New Guinea to establish a standardized national corporate image.
item.content:encoded:
Goroka-based contractor Mebiluba Service and Maintenance has commenced refurbishment and rebranding work on PNG DataCo's Kumul Submarine Cable Network landing facility in Alotau, Milne Bay.

The six-man team from Eastern Highlands has been engaged to rebrand DataCo facilities across Papua New Guinea to establish a standardized national corporate image.

Director of Mebiluba Service and Maintenance and former DataCo employee Billy Kaupa said the company, which has served as a primary contractor for DataCo since 2022, was tasked with designing and implementing the national rebranding standard.

"It was my idea to design the new branding for PNG DataCo," Kaupa said. "The previous corporate identity used Huawei's color scheme of red, white, and black, but we have transitioned to DataCo's new standard, which incorporates gold."

Kaupa confirmed that Milne Bay is the first province in the Southern region to undergo the face-lift.

"We have completed sites across the Highlands, Momase, and New Guinea Islands regions," Kaupa said. "Alotau is our initial site in the Southern region, after which we will move to Kerema, Daru, Popondetta, and conclude in Port Moresby."

Kaupa said apart from major stations in Madang, Kavieng, and Port Moresby, most DataCo facilities currently lack basic staff amenities.

Following the completion of the rebranding and refurbishment phase, the contractor will revisit each provincial site to install missing facilities, including toilets and showers.

item.title: K1m emergency allocation to fix Matugar Highway seafront
item.description: The Madang Provincial Executive Council [PEC] has approved K1 million in emergency funding to address the severe coastal erosion threatening the Matugar section along the Madang-Bogia Highway. The critical stretch of road has suffered progressive degradation due to rising sea levels and relentless wave action, leaving half the carriageway washed away and posing serious risks to commuters.
item.content:encoded:
The Madang Provincial Executive Council [PEC] has approved K1 million in emergency funding to address the severe coastal erosion threatening the Matugar section along the Madang-Bogia Highway.

The critical stretch of road has suffered progressive degradation due to rising sea levels and relentless wave action, leaving half the carriageway washed away and posing serious risks to commuters.

Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa confirmed the emergency allocation, emphasizing that part of the highway has already succumbed to shoreline erosion.

"It is now up to the Madang Provincial Administration and the Provincial Procurement Committee to fast-track the procurement process so funds can be released quickly for work to begin on saving the shoreline," Pariwa said.

The seafront underwent temporary remedial maintenance in 2024, but those structures were subsequently washed away, leaving the section exposed to continuous decay.

Pariwa stressed that constructing a durable permanent seawall is essential to secure the road infrastructure long-term.

Given that the affected section forms part of a major national highway, the Governor has also called on the Department of Works and Highways to intervene and provide national support.

item.title: Queensland medical donation to support Lutheran health services in PNG
item.description: A container of medical supplies donated by organisations and volunteers in Queensland, Australia, has been handed over to Lutheran Health Services in Lae. The supplies arrived in Papua New Guinea aboard an Australian Navy vessel and will be distributed to Lutheran hospitals and health facilities in Morobe, Madang and the Highlands.
item.content:encoded:
A container of medical supplies donated by organisations and volunteers in Queensland, Australia, has been handed over to Lutheran Health Services in Lae.

The supplies arrived in Papua New Guinea aboard an Australian Navy vessel and will be distributed to Lutheran hospitals and health facilities in Morobe, Madang and the Highlands.

The donation comes as health facilities continue to deal with shortages of essential medical supplies.

Australian Consul-General in Lae, Brenton Kanowski, said the donation was a practical way of supporting Lutheran Health Services and the communities it serves.

He said the supplies were collected and packed by volunteers in Queensland before being transported to Australia for shipment to Papua New Guinea.

The Australian Government helped facilitate the transportation of the container to Lae aboard the Australian Navy vessel.

Kanowski said the shipment showed how community organisations, volunteers and government could work together to support health services in Papua New Guinea.

The medical supplies include consumables that will be used by Lutheran hospitals and clinics across several provinces.

Lutheran Health Services provides healthcare to communities through a network of hospitals and clinics, including areas where access to government health services can be limited.

A representative of Lutheran Health Services said the supplies would help health workers continue providing care to patients and support facilities dealing with shortages.

The donation was part of wider Australian support delivered during the Australian Navy vessel's visit to Lae.

The vessel also brought two fire trucks and other supplies for community projects.

For Lutheran Health Services, the medical supplies are expected to provide immediate support to health workers and patients relying on church-run health facilities across the country.

item.title: PNG-US disaster exercise builds frontline medical skills
item.description: Papua New Guinean and United States personnel are training in basic emergency medical care as part of a joint disaster response exercise in Lae.

item.title: Marape: PNG cannot train for the workforce of 1975
item.description: Papua New Guinea must change the way it trains its young people to meet the demands of a modern economy, Prime Minister James Marape says.
